newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Algeria Islamic group said to seek Libya mediation.
newsitem.headline: Algeria Islamic group said to seek Libya mediation.

text.p: Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front has asked Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to mediate with the Algiers government to try to end their bloody confrontation, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Monday.
JANA, monitored in Tunis, quoted "sources at the World's Islamic Popular Leadership", a Libyan-sponsored grouping of Moslem movements which Gaddafi heads.

"The brother leader (Gaddafi) has received an official request from the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS ) in Algeria to mediate between it and the Algerian government to reach a political peaceful solution putting an end to bloodletting and enabling Algeria to recover its health and role in the region and the world," JANA said.

Gaddafi in 1993 referred to imprisoned FIS leaders Abbas Madani and Ali Belhaj as his "friends", but in 1994 he pledged at a meeting with Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual in Tripoli that he would do nothing to aid Algerian Moslem guerrillas.
The pledge was made after Algerian newspapers accused Tripoli of letting Moslem guerrillas cross through Libya's Sahara Desert to Algeria after training in Sudan.

Mohamed Salah Dembri, who was Algeria's foreign affairs minister in 1994, said at the time there was a commitment by Gaddafi to Zeroual not to encourage or have contact with any Algerian militant group.
The call for Gaddafi's mediation coincided with the fifth anniversary of the cancellation by Algerian military chiefs of elections that Moslem fundamentalists appeared poised to win.
The annulment plunged the North African country into violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces in which about 60,000 people have died.
